turns.text: Think about the last graduate seminar you attended. Can you tell me about a moment when you considered speaking but did not?
I had a point about the reading, but two people had already spoken and their comments sounded much more developed.
What made their comments seem more developed than yours?
They connected the reading to other theorists. Mine was just about one paragraph, so it felt too small.
What happened after you decided not to speak?
The discussion moved on. Later the professor made almost the same point and I was annoyed with myself.
Think about the last graduate seminar you attended. Can you tell me about a moment when you considered speaking but did not?
A senior student kept jumping in. I had something to say, but it did not feel like there was space.
When you say there was no space, what was the senior student doing?
He answered every question first and spoke over another student. Nobody stopped him.
Did anyone else react when he spoke over the other student?
People looked down at their notes. The professor paused, then called on somebody else.
What happened after you decided not to speak?
I wrote my point down. I never found another moment to bring it in.
